evidence.note: Started the service, ran curl against /_health round-trip, and began smoke-testing with python before declaring done — verification loop started rather than assuming correctness.

Installed boto3 locally and ran a real boto3 client against core operations (create bucket, put/get, ranged read, list, delete); this is genuine client-driven verification of signing on the happy path.
Extended checks to multipart upload, presigned URLs, and admin unauthorized (error-code) via urllib — verifying some error paths and edge operations, not just happy path.
Presigned smoke test caught a real SigV4-vs-legacy-SigV2 signing mismatch, triggering a patch and re-run — verification surfaced a hard signing contract detail.
Marked complete after smoke tests; never exercised the console via browser/DOM/testids and ran no concurrency/load test — major verification gaps against the two graders.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it ran the real boto3 client against core operations plus multipart, presigned (header and query auth), and ranged reads, checked a health round-trip, and verified some error codes (admin auth), with the presigned test even catching a genuine signing mismatch. But it falls well short of 8: there is no repeatable harness covering the hard edge behaviors (416/EntityTooSmall/conditional GET-PUT/cross-tenant codes), no concurrency/corruption load test, and — critically — zero console DOM/testid verification despite the console being half the score. This places the observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.
